content_preview.title: npm Trusted Publishing Configurations Now Expire After 48 Hours Unless Validated, and issue_comment Tokens Are Rejected
content_preview.summary: GitHub says unvalidated npm trusted publishing configurations now expire 48 hours after creation, and npm now rejects trusted publishing tokens from GitHub Actions issue_comment events.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

GitHub announced in an October 2, 2026 changelog entry that, according to the [GitHub Changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-02-unvalidated-npm-trusted-publishing-configurations-now-expire), "Unvalidated npm trusted publishing configurations now expire 48 hours after creation and can no longer authorize publishing." editor_notes.content_quality: Concise, well-structured Briefing (544 words, within 300-800). Overview, What Changed, Related changes, What We Don't Know, and a short labelled Analysis. Every bullet is attributed to the GitHub Changelog entry.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all three gzipped snapshots (source-0, source-1, source-2; all HTTP 200, ~95 KB raw HTML, extracted article text complete and not thin, so no live re-fetch was needed; suspicious_patterns null for all). source-0 (2026-10-02 'Unvalidated npm trusted publishing configurations now expire', label Retired, topic supply chain security) confirms verbatim: 'Unvalidated npm trusted publishing configurations now expire 48 hours after creation and can no longer authorize publishing.'; 'limits the risk of trusting a repository or project name that changes ownership'; 'becomes validated and exempt from expiry after its first successful publish'; identity change requires new trust relationship with fresh 48-hour window, ordinary edits do not restart the deadline; recreate to start a new window; expired configs remain visible but do not count toward per-package limits; other valid configs unaffected; 'npm also now rejects trusted publishing tokens from GitHub Actions issue_comment events, alongside the existing pull_request_target restriction'; move to push, release or workflow_dispatch. All quotes verbatim (the article's quote of the issue_comment sentence drops only the leading 'also'; text inside the quote marks begins at 'now rejects', which is verbatim). source-1 (2026-10-02 staged publishing) confirms npm stage publish for new packages, local session or granular access token incl. stage-only token, and verbatim 'enters the staged queue and requires a maintainer to promote it before that version becomes available to install' and trusted publishing configurable after creation. source-2 (2026-09-30 dist-tag) confirms opt-in 'Allow npm dist-tag' permission, verbatim 'defaults to off for both new and existing configurations, so no configuration automatically gains new capability', and 'Previously, trusted publishing covered publishing and staging, but not dist-tag operations.' Source-0's snapshot does not itself name the 'Retired' label exactly as a tag beyond the page header; it is present ('Retired October 2, 2026'). All three sources are github.blog (allowlisted). Conflict-of-interest note: GitHub is the publisher/owner of npm and of all three sources, i.e. first-party self-reporting with no independent corroboration; acceptable for a Briefing about GitHub's own policy changes because the article consistently attributes to GitHub ('GitHub announced', 'GitHub says') and states what the entry does not say, but readers should know no third-party or npm-docs verification was cited.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Dates (Oct 2, Sep 30), the 48-hour figure, event names, and all attributions check out against snapshots. One imprecision in the closing Analysis: it says GitHub is 'extending the OIDC-based flow to more tasks, such as dist-tag management and first-time package creation through staging'. Source-1 says new-package creation via npm stage publish uses a local session or granular access token, not OIDC; trusted publishing is configured only after the package exists. Dist-tag OIDC is supported by source-2. Recorded as a clarification. 'Internal links': /article/2026-05/24-npm-ships-staged-publishing-and-install-source-allowlists-in-cli-11150-requiring-human-2fa-approval-before-packages-go-live and /article/2026-10/12-pnpm-1212-adds-remote-task-caching-to-pnpm-pipeline-and-an-addmissingpeertypes-setting-12121-adds-a-tool-protocol-and-dist-tag-oidc both use the correct singular /article/<YYYY-MM>/<slug> form and both files exist; the May article covers npm CLI 11.15.0 staged publishing and the pnpm article covers dist-tag OIDC, so the descriptions are accurate. 'Covered earlier this month' is true (Oct 12). Orphan-link diff: the only external URLs in the body are the three github.blog URLs, all in article.sources and vice versa (no orphans, no unused sources). validate:content run on the repo: passes.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and factual. No sensationalism; no AI self-reference. Analysis section is brief and mostly restates the sources, apart from the clarification above.
editor_notes.originality: No existing article covers the 48-hour expiry, issue_comment restriction, or the Oct 2 new-package staged publishing change (grep over articles). The May staged-publishing article and Oct 12 pnpm article are different events and are linked as background. The August GitHub supply-chain roundup predates these changes.
concerns: Single-publisher sourcing: all three sources are GitHub changelog entries (GitHub owns npm); no independent corroboration or npm docs cited.
Analysis sentence conflates OIDC-based trusted publishing with first-time package creation via staging, which the source says uses a local session or granular token (filed as a clarification).
recommendations: Where available, cite npm docs or an independent outlet alongside first-party changelog entries.
Keep Analysis claims strictly within what the cited entries state.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, properly attributed Briefing whose headline, summary and lead are all directly supported. One minor subordinate imprecision in the Analysis section is covered by a single clarification; approved with corrections.
